messages:
olivia_sales: Hey team — ZenithBank POC kickoff today. They want a private deployment (VPC) with strict egress controls. Main asks: preserve client src IP to backend, prefer PrivateLink but worried about cross-account scale. Any quick topology recs?
noah_netops: +1. For preserving src IP we typically recommend a NAT44-preserving setup or a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For. PrivateLink endpoints terminate TCP in our VPC so original srcip won't survive unless we do TCP passthrough via a transit GW.
olivia_sales: Can you sketch the two options briefly? They care about auditability and minimal infra changes on their side.
noah_netops: Option A (PrivateLink + proxy): customer sets up interface endpoint to our ENI, traffic lands on our ALB/NLB -> we run a transparent proxy that logs client IP into XFF. Pros: least customer change. Cons: source IP not preserved on backend.
noah_netops: Option B (TGW/peering + routed path): peer TGW or VPC peering, we keep original srcip across the path. Pros: true src ip preservation, simpler for firewall rules. Cons: more operational handoff & routing config on customer.
mike_se: Pricing note: PrivateLink egress metering depends on region/endpoint type — for heavy POC traffic TGW/routed path with Reserved Dedicated may be cheaper per-token if latency SLOs hold. I can run a cost compare if you can share expected qps & avg token length.
olivia_sales: They expect ~60 qps bursty, avg 60 tokens/response. Can you ballpark?
mike_se: Rough ballpark: hosted PrivateLink egress might add ~0.5–1.5¢/request depending on egress bytes. Dedicated routed can lower per-token infra cost but has a monthly commit. I'll send a simple calc in a follow-up.
sara_sales: Security + compliance ask: customer requires whitelist of egress IPs for allowlisting in their firewall. Can we provide static IPs for POC?
noah_netops: For PrivateLink we can provide the interface endpoint ENI IPs, but they're per-AZ and can change on redeploy. For stable outbound IPs use NAT Gateway or egress EIPs on a transit VPC — we can allocate static EIPs for the POC.
noah_netops: Example firewall snippet for them to allow outbound to our egress (replace X.X.X.X):
```
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to X.X.X.X/32 port 443
allow udp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 53
```
noah_netops: And if they want source IP preservation over TGW, they'd allow our service subnets: 172.20.0.0/22 -> ports 443, 1026 (health)
tim_security: Quick security checklist: TLS 1.2+, mTLS between customer on-prem proxy and our edge if requested, KMS for keys at rest, audit logs forwarded to customer S3 (read-only) or we provide SOC2 + pen-test report. We also support IP allowlist, FQDN allowlist for hosts used.
olivia_sales: They also sent a network security questionnaire. Tim — can you fill the network section? I'll attach the doc.
tim_security: I can do a draft today. Key answers: we do not persist plaintext customer payloads in logs by default, we support VPC endpoints and private deployments, we offer HSM/KMS integration, and can enable packet-level audit for Dedicated if needed.
sara_sales: Timeline question: can we get static eips + initial PrivateLink/proxy test within 3 business days?
noah_netops: Yes for a POC we can carve out 2 EIPs and stand up the interface endpoints + nginx proxy in a spare AZ in ~48 hours. TGW setup with customer routing will take longer — expect ~5 business days with customer network team.
mike_se: I'll attach a very light cost comparison in the channel after lunch.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: private-poc/proxy/zenithbank -> staging at 2024-03-28T14:30Z by noah_netops :rocket:
olivia_sales: Perfect — next steps: (1) mike to post cost compare, (2) tim to draft network section of questionnaire, (3) noah to provision EIPs + endpoint for POC, (4) olivia to sync with ZenithBank netsec. I'll confirm meeting tomorrow. :thumbsup:
noah_netops: I'll also post the exact EIP values and the temporary SG rules once provisioned.
tim_security: Ping me if they require formal DAST/VAPT before POC.
sara_sales: Thanks all — tagging @zenithbank-ct to keep them looped in once we have EIP list.
olivia_sales: Thanks team!
